messages.text: Furious Arteta rages over 'unacceptable' Sunderland penalty call

metadata.summary: A furious Mikel Arteta described Sunderland's penalty in Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light as "unacceptable".
metadata.content: Mikel Arteta rages at Sunderland penalty decision after Arsenal win at Stadium of Light: 'This cannot happen' | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Mikel Arteta rages at Sunderland penalty decision after Arsenal win at Stadium of Light: 'This cannot happen' Mikel Arteta was left furious by the award of Sunderland's penalty during Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light, saying such decisions can cost a side a Premier League title; David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's spot kick as Gunners claimed a fourth straight win Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Saturday 12 September 2026 23:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Was Ezri Konsa's challenge on Dan Ballard enough for Sunderland to be awarded a penalty? A furious Mikel Arteta described Sunderland's penalty in Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light as "unacceptable". The home side were awarded a spot kick in the 54th minute when defender Ezri Konsa was adjudged to have held Sunderland's Dan Ballard by referee John Brooks. "The referee's call of penalty to Sunderland for a holding offence by Konsa on Ballard was checked and confirmed by VAR," said a statement published by the Premier League Match Centre. The statement continued by quoting the interaction between on-pitch referee Brooks and the VAR.
